messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for streaming.generate in us-west-2. p95=420ms -> 1.1s, p99=980ms -> 2.3s. error rate stable. Auto-mitigations triggered: fallback routing to model-variant B, prefetch jobs started. Escalating to #incidents.
alice.sre: seeing correlated increase in streaming stall counts and backend paging. dashboards: stream-tail-stalls spike at 22:03 UTC. Investigating cache hitrate for prefix-hash v4 rollout.
bob-runtime: rolling logs show cache miss ratio for prefix cache jump from 12% -> 68% on affected pods. Likely mismatch in prefix hashing after recent rollout (prefix-hash:v4) — keys not matching new salt.
carla-eng: confirmed — deployment prefix-hash:v4 included a salted namespace change. Some edge nodes still on v3 (partial rollout). Mix of v3/v4 causes dramatic low hit due to namespace misalignment.
dave-support: customer impact: two customers reported streaming stalls and delayed responses in their sessions (no 5xx). They're seeing repeated re-requests; raising potential downstream retries.
emma-pm: which customers? label them and severity. Need short customer-facing note if impact persists >30m.
frank-oncall: preflight checklist — can we fallback traffic to dedicated cache-read path (v3) or force routing to fully rolled-back variant?
bob-runtime: immediate mitigation options:
- rollback prefix-hash:v4 (fast but needs deploy window) 
- force routing of all streaming.generate to model-variant B (already partial fallback) and increase spec for prefetch/warmers
- run targeted cache-warm for hot prefixes (script below)

Faster is to force rollout rollback for the hashing lib (patch to revert salt) and trigger cache-warmers.

Command for targeted warmers (run on control plane):
```
# run warmers for top 500 hot prefixes from telemetry
./tools/prefetch_warmer --source telemetry/hot_prefixes_5m.json --parallel 40 --region us-west-2
```

carla-eng: warming only helps if keys line up — if v4 keys are different, warming v3 won't help clients routed to v4. We need either full rollback or universal rehash and coordinated rolling restart.
alice.sre: quick telemetry snapshot: top affected prefixes show TTL+cache-miss traces. Paging counts up 4x on affected shards. Paging implies increased IO and added tail latency for streaming tails.
lisa-cust-eng: internal note — Customer A (enterprise) seeing p99 ~2.1s for streaming sessions. They're preparing a support escalation if >45m. Keep them updated.
frank-oncall: action plan (immediate):
1) throttle rollout — pause prefix-hash:v4 rollout (stop further pods adopting) — CARLA to stop webhook
2) rollback prefix salt in next 10m (carla)
3) enable forced routing to model-variant B for streaming.generate for affected orgs and edge clusters (bob)
4) start targeted cache warmers for v3 keys to recover hitrate where nodes still v3 (alice)
5) monitor p95/p99 and paging IO every 2m (incident-bot)

carla-eng: paused rollout webhook. initiating rollback patch for hashing lib. ETA ~7m for canary deploy then full rollout revert.
bob-runtime: applying forced routing rule for streaming.generate in us-west-2 for high-traffic orgs. ACLs set. Will also increase prefetch worker concurrency from 8->24 for next 15m.

dave-support: drafting interim customer note: "We're investigating increased latency for streaming responses in us-west-2. We have mitigation steps in progress and will update within 30 minutes."
emma-pm: please include expected ETA and contact for urgent escalations.
frank-oncall: rolling metrics — p95 down to 510ms, p99 to 1.6s after forced routing/partial warmers; still above SLO for some customers. Paging IO trending down but not fully normalized.
carla-eng: revert to v3 completed on 60% of nodes. need 100% for stable cache hitrate; continuing rolling restart for remaining nodes. no config drift observed beyond salt.
alice.sre: verification: cache hitrate improved from 32% -> 72% on nodes reverted. streaming tail-stalls decreased by ~60% on reverted fleet.
lisa-cust-eng: updated Customer A with 25m ETA and mitigation summary; they acknowledged and de-escalated for now.
frank-oncall: preparing handoff in 45m to night oncall. Summary to include: cause = partial prefix-hash:v4 rollout with salting change -> cross-version key mismatch -> cache miss surge -> paging and tail latency; mitigations = paused rollout, rollback to v3, forced routing to variant B, cache warmers; current status = p99 trending down but still ~1.2s in pockets; next steps = finish fleet revert, monitor, re-run canary with backward-compatible salt if re-deploying.
carla-eng: leaving logs/commands and revert PR link in thread. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/PR-8123 revert prefix-hash:v4

frank-oncall: handoff note for next oncall (@frank-oncall -> @harry-night):
- watch p99 and paging IO for 2 hours
- ensure no new rollout of prefix-hash:v4
- if p99 > 1.5s for >10m, escalate paging team and consider full service rollback
- keep Customer A updated every 30m until stable

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation progressing. p95=420ms, p99=1.2s, paging IO down 45%. Next automated checkpoint in 10m."
